scope: Constructor, struct, tuple, grouped, literal, identifier and or-pattern syntax
obligations: Single identifiers remain ambiguous between a binding and a constant or constructor until actual source name resolution.
Bare tuple patterns require a checked tuple layout. Positional fields on a tuple-struct do not turn that struct into a tuple.
Constructor record-versus-positional style is a source layout obligation; JavaScript field names alone do not prove Rust constructor syntax.
A pattern projection plan does not establish copy, move, borrow, alias or drop behavior. The source frontend must establish those obligations before emission.
Irrefutability must be proved for function parameter and plain let-binding contexts before body lowering.
implementedSyntax: named record fields and final rest
validation: Node and Bun validate independent syntax spans, actual checked projection layouts, literal domains, exhaustiveness and source refusals without Rust execution.
